blocks.text: Isaiah 38 belongs to a book that includes prophetic speech, first-person material, third-person narration, sign actions, and royal narratives. The book presents Isaiah son of Amoz as its named prophet, yet scholars also study its received form as the result of a long process of collection and editorial development; no detailed reconstruction has gained consensus. This makes it important to attend closely to the form of each passage and establish its speakers from the passage itself.
